claims.text: Circular OC 186A, titled 'Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)', was issued by NPCI on September 10, 2026, to extend UPI Tap & Pay via NFC from QR codes to PoS terminals for contactless payments.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are restricted exclusively to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit user consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit user consent for enabling the feature, while also providing users the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs are required to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals within their acquiring network.
Device lock must be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per-transaction limit is capped at INR 5000, above which additional authentication factors may be required.
UPI Application Providers must present UPI Tap & Pay as a standalone feature via a dedicated call-to-action, not embedded within other services or menus.

Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for these transactions must follow extant UPI guidelines, along with RBI guidelines on Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation.
Remitter Banks must validate the user's account for feature enablement before processing each transaction, while users can set their own limits within the INR 5000 ceiling.

Detailed functional, technical, and operational requirements are to be found in applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Documents, Technical Specifications, and other NPCI instructions issued from time to time.

claims.text: Circular OC 186A, titled 'Enhancement - UPI Tap & Pay on Point of Sale (PoS)', was issued by NPCI on September 10, 2026, to extend UPI Tap & Pay via NFC from QR codes to PoS terminals for contactless payments.
UPI Tap & Pay transactions on PoS terminals are restricted exclusively to Person-to-Merchant (P2M) transactions.
Payee PSPs must enable UPI Tap & Pay only on NFC-enabled PoS terminals certified in accordance with PCI PTS / CPOC standards.
UPI Application Providers and PSP Banks must obtain explicit user consent after each device binding operation before allowing further transactions.
Members and UPI Application Providers must obtain explicit user consent for enabling the feature, while also providing users the ability to opt out at any time.
Payee PSPs are required to integrate the Point-of-Sale Common Library for UPI (PoS CL) on all PoS terminals within their acquiring network.
Device lock must be enabled as a prerequisite for activating UPI Tap & Pay, and the device must be unlocked at the time of initiating a transaction.
The per-transaction limit is capped at INR 5000, above which additional authentication factors may be required.
UPI Application Providers must present UPI Tap & Pay as a standalone feature via a dedicated call-to-action, not embedded within other services or menus.

Settlement, reconciliation, dispute management, and Online Dispute Resolution (ODR) for these transactions must follow extant UPI guidelines, along with RBI guidelines on Turn Around Time (TAT) and customer compensation.
Remitter Banks must validate the user's account for feature enablement before processing each transaction, while users can set their own limits within the INR 5000 ceiling.

Detailed functional, technical, and operational requirements are to be found in applicable UPI Tap & Pay Feature Documents, Technical Specifications, and other NPCI instructions issued from time to time.

sources.text: 1001A, B wing, 10th Floor, The Capital, Bandra-Kurla Complex, Bandra (East), Mumbai - 400 051 CIN: U74990MH2008NPL189067 Circular: NPCI/2017-18/PD/004 August 10, 2017 To, All RuPay Acquiring Member Banks Integration of Bharat QR with UPI credentials Dear All, As per the direction received from Reserve Bank of India in October 2016, NPCI and International card schemes jointly worked towards implementing common interoperable QR code based card payment solution namely “Bharat QR”. Bharat QR was launched on 20th February, 2017. Further, under the guidance of Indian Bank Association (IBA), NPCI had facilitated to integrate UPI credentials (Virtual Payment Address (VPA), Account + IFSC & Aadhaar number) as a part of Bharat QR standards. In this regard, NPCI had released technical specifications (Merchant QR Code Specification V 4.0) to integrate UPI credentials in Bharat QR to all RuPay acquiring member banks on 18th May, 2017. It may be noted that RuPay acquiring member banks have already started the development to integrate UPI credentials with Bharat QR and various banks are under certification with NPCI. We request all RuPay acquiring member banks to comply with Merchant QR Code Specifications V 4.0 and ensure that all Bharat QR deployed post 15th Sep 2017 should contain UPI credentials. Yours truly, Dilip Asbe Chief Operating Officer

sources.text: fs Conroe =) NPCI/UPI/OC no.199/2024-25 25" June 2024 To, All Members, UPI (Unified Payment Interface) Dear Sir/Madam, Subject: Update to NPCI CL version 1.8 or above UPI has become a preferred digital payment mode across the country. It provides ease of use, convenience and superior user experience with security and interoperability. To ensure the safety and security of the UPI systems, NPCI constantly reviews the security checks of all components in the UPI ecosystem and regularly upgrades them to address evolving threats in cyber landscape. There are security checks implemented as part of the code embedded in the Common Library (CL) along with the feature release to enhance user experience on UPI platforms. Integration of latest versions of CL is important to ensure enhanced security and safety in UPI ecosystem. With this objective, NPCI will be retiring the support for CL prior to Version 1.8 after 30% September 2024. To ensure compliance PSP Banks shall certify and enable CL 1.8 or above and their respective UPI Apps shall integrate the latest version of CL within their application, on or before 30% September 2024. Members are requested to take note of this compliance and communicate it to relevant stakeholders and their respective partners. Yours sincerely, SD/- Kunal Kalawatia Chief of Products 1001A, The Capital, B Wing, 10* Floor, Bandra Kurla Complex,
